**Order filled:** 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801, under the $10,000 per-order cap; total day spend $9,801 of the $20,000 limit; no funds moved out of the account).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask), then bought 44 shares of AAPL with a limit at $222.75 — essentially at the market, inside the mandate's price-proximity requirement. The key figure the task asked for: **Apple's net income for fiscal 2024 was $93,736 million**, down 3.4% from $96,995 million in fiscal 2023. That decline is not an operating deterioration — it is almost entirely the one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge from the European Commission's State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7% a year earlier). Underneath it, the business improved: net sales rose 2% to $391,035 million, operating income grew 7.8% to $123,216 million, Services revenue climbed 13% to $96,169 million at a 73.9% gross margin, diluted EPS was $6.08, and operating cash flow was a robust $118,254 million, with $140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities. I sized the position at roughly $9.8k — a modest, mandate-compliant starter position rather than a full allocation — because the headline net income and EPS figures are still optically depressed by the tax charge and the stock is near its recent highs, leaving room to add on any pullback while staying within today's $20,000 total budget.
